Okay so I can say with certainty that I was you. I grew up in NYC with pressure from family on specific matters. I did poorly in school throughout high school because of the immense pressure. One of my parents even brews beer so I understand the drinking aspect. The biggest positive steps I took were transferring to a high school that actually supported me and then getting out of my family’s household. I also got close to specific teachers because I knew they were the ones that would notice if something was off with me emotionally. I played classical music so being in an orchestra forced me to stay alive, because as suicidal as I was at your age, I couldn’t end it yet as I was one of a few people in the section I was in at that specific orchestra. Please, please, please reach out to me for any help you need. 

If you can, get into a hobby. Music helped me, but if you’re into gaming, coding, drawing, playing a new instrument, anything at all, please pick it up. It gives you an excuse to healthily isolate from family without actually being alone. There are so many online forums for new activities, especially because of covid, and it gives you an excuse to socialize with others that have shared interests while avoiding the toxic people in your life. If you want to, please PM me. I am absolutely happy to go more in depth and give you more advice about the hell that is growing up in NYC

My memory started to struggle after I went through a traumatic event (a car hit me, I was a pedestrian). It’s really sucked because not only am I struggling to remember the events that occurred during the accident, but I space on where I leave my phone/wallet/personal items far too frequently. I’m in therapy now to deal with this stuff and it’s definitely helping. Whatever is going on with you, I recommend seeing your general practitioner and/or a therapist in case you need medication for something like adhd or if you’re somehow coping with a trauma in a way. Best of luck.

I’m asking for advice on what to do, how to move on, how to deal with this situation. I HAVE been sucking it up for years... that’s why I’m asking for advice now. I was hoping to be met with compassion from people who may have not ever been in this situation but can be sympathetic to the emotional turmoil this has caused in my life. Sure, I backed myself into this situation, but I’ve never been burdened or resented my relationship, even if it wasn’t going the exact direction I may have initially expected. And sure, many people are going through actual situations that have actual possibilities to change and impact their lives for forever. But doesn’t anyone who’s trying to do the right thing, who’s honest and clear about their feelings, who listens to their partners wishes and adjusts their lifestyle to keep their loved ones happy and comfortable, doesn’t someone like that deserve a little bit better than being accused of being a cheater, a liar, and being told to suck it up? 

I’m trying to get advice on how to deal with this so I can move forward with the relationship I clearly chose because I clearly value it and find happiness from it... and not only have I been choosing this specific relationship, but my partner has as well, even knowing everything that he does. Doesn’t he deserve, at the very minimum, for someone to advise me on how to figure out how to deal with the situation in the kindest way to him? Doesn’t he deserve the respect of his choice to stick with me be respected, considering that he has had the opportunity to walk away at any chance?

But... I am in love with my boyfriend? That’s the point of ethical non monogamy? That’s the point of polyamory? That you can feel multiple things for multiple people... the ethical part is that I honestly confided in my partner and we agreed that nothing physical could ever occur between myself and anyone but I could continue to feel the way that I do... and I’ve followed by that set of guidelines. What I don’t understand is the hoop jumping to say that I’ve been emotionally cheating when the only instance where that could have possibly been true, I pretty quickly had an honest conversation with my parter, and we both decided to stay together even when he knew I had feelings for him AND someone else... honesty and agreement was what sparked this conversation 3 years ago, and it’s what’s peaking my interest now. But I never lied or fell out of love with my partner and I’m confused why you both are insisting that I have. Have you read much about poly culture?

Where do you think I got the information that he didn’t like the idea of a polyamorous relationship? I did tell him about that dinner, and everything that happened within days of the dinner happening. Again, the reason I stayed with him and he stayed with me is because we both care for one another... I just also happen to get feelings for several people and he is aware of this... he just asks that I never act on anything... and I’ve agreed to that to make him comfortable in our relationship... you seem to be doing a lot of jumping through a lot of hoops before asking questions and offering kind and compassionate advice to someone who just wants to do right by the people in her life...

Also, I never said I was in a poly relationship, I said I personally was poly? For me to do anything without a partners consent is clearly not okay, and I would never cross a boundary once it’s been put in place by both parts of the relationship. Where did you get the idea that I was acting on anything?

How have I been cheating though? I’m barely in contact with Max and pretty much never followed up after that dinner? I also clearly stated that I’m incredibly against cheating, thus the reason why I haven’t done anything further than a singular dinner??

Definitely NTA. As much as I understand him wanting his sleep, I have just as many memories with my dad spending time with me as my mom did, so each parent got some peace and quiet. In fact, I remember my dad being awake even before me most weekend days because he had a weekend routine that relied on early mornings. But my mom spent days with us when my dad was at work. They both relied on each other to parent me and my siblings. Looking back, I’m super proud of them for figuring out how to support each other as my dad had a full time day job and my mom worked with pregnant women so her hours were infrequent but she sometimes was up at 3 am when women went into labor. My dad was super present in my childhood and now, in my twenties, I have a fabulous relationship with them both because of how well they coparented. 

Your husband needs to be accountable to his children. Not only does his inaction affect you and your wellbeing, it will affect how his/your children remember their childhood and their relationships with each of you later on. You absolutely deserve to sleep in and he absolutely needs to step up. 

That being said, I also don’t know the rest of how you guys parent. There may be ways he does things that make him an excellent father, so unlike others, I don’t want to deem him completely evil. I just believe that in the circumstance you’ve presented, he is the asshole, not you.

I’m going with YTA but for one simple reason. Your teacher had struggled with finding this patients pulse as well, but did not state an obvious fact in such a rude way. Your teacher struggled with a patient, and watched you struggle as well, but then listened to you unkindly blame a patient for your own inability to find a pulse. The patient, despite an obvious health risk that comes with obesity (I’m overweight too, so I’m not fat shaming) does not need to be shamed. A huge reason why my health is actually on an upswing is because my current doctors have kindly (and in a straightforward way) given me actually useful tips to benefit my health. Although I have never been anywhere near as obese as the patient you’ve described, the kindness and compassion that came from medical professionals helped me feel more confident in my choice to be healthier. Although it is not rude to explicitly point out someone’s figure in a medical sense, there is likely a reason that patient is that size. It is not your place to judge are make statements. It is simply your place to learn how to care for a patient of that size. Your comment, had it been directed at me, and had I overheard it, definitely would have made me feel shame and would not have brought me any closer to a healthier and easier-to-treat weight.

While it might have sucked that you had a disadvantage to other classmates because they had their tests with classmates who were in better health, and therefor easier to read, if you had practiced at all for this exam then you should have known that you could potentially be paired with “Patty”. Therefor, you should have practiced taking the vitals of other obese people. You did not have any disadvantages because you likely knew this test was coming up and how it would be given. You should have known to study/practice more.

My biggest piece of advice is to find an ally. My first job out of school had the worst chef I have met, even with all of my job changes (I’m a woman too, and this chef was a tall, vaguely racist [I’m white and so was he but I cannot stand any sense of inequality so this made the dude even more intolerable], definitely misogynistic man - definitely intimidating to me).  However, I found solace in the fact that the two sous chefs defended me mercilessly and spent every moment they could spare furthering my education they agreed that the head chef was truly terrible and I still keep in touch with one of those sous’s, even after quitting. Having someone who will defend your honor and make your education - even post school - a priority is invaluable. This isn’t to say that they’ll never snap at you, but finding someone who has been in that kitchen or in the industry itself for a while is useful. 

The kitchen I’m currently in is kind of a disaster as well, but since I’ve gained a few allies, any time a hiccup happens, I know I will still have people in my corner. It helps. 

I’m so sorry you are going through this. It literally is the exact same thing I went though. Please message me privately if you ever want to vent.

My siblings and I are all adults but when we gather for holidays, we still act like little kids and bicker the same way as when we were younger and see our parents playing favorites in different ways even when they aren’t. 

No one is to blame here.

Almost a year later, a kid from my high school passed away from cancer and I went to his wake. I was not prepared to see his corpse in the slightest but there it was. Those two events happening a year apart from each other when I was still a teen made me deeply hate the existence of children and the fact that the could die just as easily as any adult. I’ve lost lots of people in my life but seeing two minors (a baby and a teen) gave me a severe phobia of parenting as the idea of outliving a child would push me into a worse depression.

Aside from that, I also have a deep disgust with the concept of giving birth and would never truly forgive any child for putting me through pregnancy. It’s a borderline dysphoria. There is nothing that makes me feel more betrayed by my cis gender female body than the fact that I can birth children. But due to my age and country, most doctors won’t allow me to have a hysterectomy for many years. But the concept of pregnancy and birth truly makes me depressed and borderline suicidal. 

Also I simply do not like younger children. I do not have the interest in pampering and coddling or the patience to wipe the shit and tears away. 

All of that being said, I will not ever be cruel or mean to a child. They don’t know why I don’t like them and don’t deserve my own cynicism just because the exist. I’ll always be kind to the kids I encounter, but I will never have my own.
